Circumspect

SUR-kum-spekt · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Circumspect is carefully considers all options before acting.

The circumspect investor researched every detail of the company before committing any money.

Worked Example

The lawyer remained circumspect throughout the negotiation, never revealing more than she strictly had to.

Circumspect describes someone who is watchful and cautious, weighing risks and consequences carefully before speaking or acting.

How Circumspect Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

cautious

cautious: careful to avoid risk

wary

wary: on guard against possible danger

Antonyms

reckless

reckless: acting without care for consequences

careless

careless: not paying attention to risk

How Strong Is It? — careful → circumspect → guarded

careful vs. circumspect

careful vs. circumspect: Being careful just means you're paying reasonable attention.

guarded vs. circumspect

guarded vs. circumspect: Being guarded goes further, actively protecting yourself and revealing very little.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — circum-

prefix — circum-: around (Latin)

root — spect

root — spect: to look (Latin (specere))

Put it together

Put it together: circum- ("around") + spect ("to look") = to look around carefully before acting.

Use the root in a new word: inspect

Use the root in a new word: inspect: The same root gives us "inspect," to look closely into something -- both words share this Latin root for looking.

Root Check

Word Choice

Circumspect is a fairly formal, measured word -- it suits careful writing or a serious discussion of someone's caution, but 'careful' would sound more natural in casual chat.
